rationale: values stay under method-labelled variables; methods are combined only in an opt-in pooled product, and only where a rule below allows it

conditions: same structure definition (grey matter vs grey plus white; same parts); same hemisphere basis; adults
rationale: totals agree where tested side by side
evidence: Bahney & von Bartheld 2014 J Neurosci Methods 222:165 doi:10.1016/j.jneumeth.2013.11.002 (fractionator about 100% of stereology, nuclei per mg of primate white matter); Bahney & von Bartheld 2018 Anat Rec 301:697 doi:10.1002/ar.23728 (spinal-cord totals not significantly different); Herculano-Houzel, von Bartheld, Miller & Kaas 2015 Cell Tissue Res 360:29 doi:10.1007/s00441-015-2127-6

rationale: stereology can score small neurons as glia; the fractionator misses NeuN-negative neurons
evidence: Bahney & von Bartheld 2018 Anat Rec 301:697 doi:10.1002/ar.23728 (macaque spinal cord: 69.4 vs 27.4 million neurons); von Bartheld, Bahney & Herculano-Houzel 2016 J Comp Neurol 524:3865 doi:10.1002/cne.24040

quantity: glia-neuron ratio (GNR) vs non-neuron to neuron ratio (nNNR)
conditions: a GNR may be derived from an nNNR only with a stated endothelial fraction, and is then marked derived (rule derive_flagged)
rationale: the fractionator's non-neuronal cells include endothelial cells (12-30% of non-neuronal cells)
evidence: Bahney & von Bartheld 2018 Anat Rec 301:697 doi:10.1002/ar.23728

methods_involved: per mm3 of sections vs per mg (fractionator)
rationale: different bases; section densities depend on shrinkage and the reference volume (reference trap)
evidence: von Bartheld, Bahney & Herculano-Houzel 2016 J Comp Neurol 524:3865 doi:10.1002/cne.24040

quantity: cell density per mm2 of section or per field
rationale: depends on section thickness and cell size
evidence: von Bartheld, Bahney & Herculano-Houzel 2016 J Comp Neurol 524:3865 doi:10.1002/cne.24040

quantity: neurons under 1 mm2 of cortical surface
methods_involved: STEREO_* vs IF_FLOW or IF_HEMOCYTOMETER with measured surface
rationale: same quantity, but the two approaches reached opposite conclusions about uniformity
evidence: Carlo & Stevens 2013 PNAS 110:1488 doi:10.1073/pnas.1221398110; Herculano-Houzel, Collins, Wong, Kaas & Lent 2008 PNAS 105:12593 doi:10.1073/pnas.0805417105

rationale: model-based counts are kept off by default and never pooled
evidence: von Bartheld, Bahney & Herculano-Houzel 2016 J Comp Neurol 524:3865 doi:10.1002/cne.24040

rationale: a labelled subpopulation is a different quantity
